message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic, modern, and cult‑favorite horror films you might enjoy:

| # | Title | Year | Why it’s worth watching |
|---|-------|------|--------------------------|
| 1 | **The Shining** | 1980 | A masterclass in psychological dread, with iconic imagery and a chilling performance by Jack Nicholson. |
| 2 | **Hereditary** | 2018 | A deeply unsettling family drama that turns into a nightmare, featuring Toni Collette’s powerhouse acting. |
| 3 | **Get Out** | 2017 | A smart, socially conscious horror that blends satire with genuine terror. |
| 4 | **The Conjuring** | 2013 | A modern supernatural thriller that revitalized the haunted‑house genre. |
| 5 | **Midsommar** | 2019 | A daylight horror that subverts expectations with its unsettling folk‑tale vibe. |
| 6 | **A Quiet Place** | 2018 | Tension built around silence, with a strong emotional core. |
| 7 | **It Follows** | 2014 | A fresh take on the “invisible stalker” trope, with a creepy, relentless vibe. |
| 8 | **The Babadook** | 2014 | A psychological horror that explores grief and motherhood. |
| 9 | **The Ring** | 2002 | A modern retelling of a Japanese horror classic, with a haunting atmosphere. |
|10 | **The Cabin in the Woods** | 2012 | A meta‑horror that plays with genre conventions while delivering solid scares. |
|11 | **Suspiria** (2018) | 2018 | A visually striking remake of the 1977 classic, with a haunting score and strong performances. |
|12 | **The Witch** | 2015 | A slow‑burning, atmospheric horror set in 1630s New England. |
|13 | **Paranormal Activity** | 2007 | A low‑budget found‑footage film that still manages to keep you on edge. |
|14 | **The Others** | 2001 | A gothic thriller with a twist ending that keeps you guessing. |
|15 | **The Exorcist** | 1973 | A timeless classic that still feels terrifying today. |

Feel free to pick based on your mood—whether you want psychological dread, supernatural chills, or a fresh twist on old tropes. Enjoy the fright!
